claim: At z=0, exact known-channel correction has variance overhead R(p)=(1-2p)^-2 at equal independent shot count.
discrimination: Compare corrected noisy measurement variance with ideal measurement variance under the same z and N.
evidence_sequence: Analytic variance quantifies the cost of inversion.
main_text_location: Synthetic estimator example, sampling-cost discussion near the overhead table.

layout.reason: Final 85 x 76 mm PDF and PNG inspected: labels/markers legible, no clipping, near-square axes retain the scalar comparison.

style_semantics: Blue solid curve: exact theory. Open circles: four specified theory evaluations. Black dashed line: ideal ratio 1. Logarithmic y axis.

panels.claim: Correction overhead increases as p approaches one half.
panels.observable_units: Dimensionless variance ratio at z=0, same shot count N.
panels.conditions: Known fixed 0<=p<1/2; independent identically prepared single-qubit Z measurements; displayed range 0<=p<=.45.
panels.processed_source: values.csv: 451 evenly spaced p values and exact formula evaluations.
panels.transforms: Analytic evaluation; no smoothing, fit or aggregation.
panels.comparison: Ideal same-N estimator at z=0 has ratio 1.
panels.uncertainty: Not applicable: analytic variance ratio, not sampled observations; no invented error bars.
panels.challenge: Known p and independent shots are necessary; the ratio shown is for z=0, not a state-independent variance ratio.
panels.visual_encoding: Near-square scalar axes; logarithmic overhead axis resolves 1 to100; dashed ideal baseline.
